newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL EXPORT CREDIT DEMAND SURGES.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL EXPORT CREDIT DEMAND SURGES.

text.p: Demand for export financing surged in Brazil in the first half of the year following new rules for granting so-called Proex funds, an official said.
Mauricio Cortes, secretary of foreign trade at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, told reporters late Monday that the government had authorized $427 million in Proex funding in June.
The June figure brought export financing for the first half of 1997 to $4.1 billion compared with just $729 million in the same period a year before.
Cortes said Proex financing was approved for 1,781 export operations in the January-June period.

In June, funding was approved for 331 operations involving 65 companies. The goods were shipped to 49 countries, including six for the first time -- India, Romania, Norway, Senegal, Panama and Nicaragua.
Faced with a widening trade gap, Brazil in April this year extended the number of products eligible for Proex financing and made it easier for firms to apply by removing some red tape.
